hints: Before reversing a group, check that k nodes actually exist.
Reversing one group is ordinary list reversal - but you must reconnect it to what comes before and after.
Track group_prev (node before the group) and group_next (node after). Reverse with prev starting at group_next.

insight.mnemonic: Count k, flip k, stitch both ends.
insight.oneLiner: For each full group: find its kth node, reverse it with prev = the node after the group, then hook group_prev to the new first node.
insight.pattern: Sublist reversal with a dummy and group anchors

recall.a: The node right after the group (group_next).
recall.q: What does prev start as when reversing a group?

recall.a: The group's original first node, now its last.

insight.why: Starting the reversal's prev at group_next attaches the reversed group's tail automatically; one more assignment fixes its head.

oneLiner: For each full group: find its kth node, reverse it with prev = the node after the group, then hook group_prev to the new first node.

pitfalls.explain: Leave a final group with fewer than k nodes untouched - check that k nodes exist first.
pitfalls.title: Reversed the final short group

pitfalls.explain: Connect group_prev to the new first node and the old first node to group_next.
pitfalls.title: Lost nodes while relinking

solutions.idea: Reverse chunks of the value list and write them back. Gets the right output but doesn't move nodes.
solutions.name: Rewrite the values

footnotes.text: Reversing a sublist in place needs four handles: the node before the group, the group's first and last nodes, and the node after it. Lose one and the list falls apart.

solutions.idea: Find each full group, reverse it, and stitch it between its neighbours.
solutions.name: Reverse each group in place

# Definition for singly-linked list.

class Solution:
    def reverseKGroup(self, head: Optional[ListNode], k: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
statement:
Given the `head` of a linked list, reverse the nodes **`k` at a time** and return the modified list. If the number of nodes left at the end is less than `k`, leave them in their original order.

You must rearrange the nodes themselves - don't just rewrite the values.
title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
